cohort: The study included 90 pregnant women aged 18 to 40 years with singleton pregnancies.
finding: Cervical elastography shows promise as a predictive tool for pre-term delivery, offering moderate sensitivity (68%) and specificity (72%), with enhanced accuracy noted in nulliparous women and those with shorter cervical length.
cross-section timing: Cervical elastography measurements were obtained between 18 to 24 weeks of gestation.
gest_age: 18-24 weeks of gestation (at measurement); average 20 weeks at recruitment
